newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 11.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 11.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

ROME - Formula One motor racing supremo Bernie Ecclestone says in an Italian newspaper interview that a tobacco sponsorship ban will hit the sport's finances and could lead to cutbacks in races or their transfer to Asia. "Very few other multinationals are capable of investing as much as cigarette producers," he says.

LONDON - Companies that introduce expensive makeovers of their corporate images are taking a risk, but it's often a bigger risk to do nothing, corporate identity specialists say. "It is hugely expensive to launch a new identity but sometimes companies have no choice if they want to be perceived as modern forward thinking organisations," Richard Watson, a consultant to the design industry, says.

LONDON - Women are finding it hard to land top jobs at British advertising agencies -- organisations they say are dominated by so-called male values -- but are managing to climb higher up the ranks than ever before, a study by the Women's Advertising Club of London says.
HAMBURG - Germany's central advertising association criticises the European Commission for failing to provide a clearer policy for what it calls the grey area of comparative advertising law.

LONDON - Saatchi & Saatchi Advertising launches what it claims is Britain's first cause-related marketing unit. The Saatchi & Saatchi Cause Connection will find and establish profitable links between charities and businesses.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

STRASBOURG, France - The European Parliament gives final approval to new European Union broadcasting legislation. The "television without frontiers" law will guarantee that European viewers can see major sporting events when exclusive rights are snapped up by pay television channels.

PARIS - Jean-Pierre Cottet, managing director of French public television channel France 2, says his station does not need to run a "stupid race" for audience share with rival private TV channel TF1. "Being under that would lead us to lose our status as a popular channel," he says.
BUDAPEST - Investors in Hungary's media market will have to submit their bids for two nationwide FM channel concessions on September 8, the national radio and television body ORTT says.

OSAKA, Japan - Japanese consumer electronics giant Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd says it plans to sell antennas and set-top boxes for the Japanese satellite broadcasting venture Japan Sky Broadcasting Corp, which is due to start a 100-channel service next spring.

PARIS - French media group Havas appoints Eric Licoys as senior executive vice president with responsibility for implementing strategic decisions taken by the board and the company's chairman, Pierre Dauzier.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PURCHASE, New York - PepsiCo Inc names executives to run its three fast-food restaurant divisions when the divisions are spun off into a single separate company later this year. Mike Rawlings will run Pizza Hut, Jeff Moody will head KFC and Peter Waller will run Taco Bell. The new company, which has yet to be named, will have more than 29,000 restaurants in 95 countries.

LONDON - British Airways Plc unveils a new 60 million pound ($100 million) corporate image, which features ethnic art from around the world. Chief executive Robert Ayling says BA wants to become more international in its image while exploiting the best of the British Airways brand, as it presses ahead with ambitions to become a global airline.

TURIN - Italy's new car incentive buying scheme is helping boost car sales in the nation's poor south more than in its richer northern regions car importers association Unrae says. The incentive scheme financed by the government and the car industry offers owners of cars over 10 years old price discounts if they trade them in for new cars.
WOLFSBURG, Germany - German carmaker Volkswagen AG says its vehicle sales for the first five months of 1997 rose 9.2 percent to 1.8 million units.
COPENHAGEN - Danish brewer Carlsberg says it is in talks with Lithuanian beer-maker Utenos.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

NEW YORK - Condom makers are reaching out to intrigue the youth market with fun, games, entertainment -- as well as the safety factor. Ansell Personal Products, which makes the Lifestyles brand, has hired Howard Stern, the feisty, radio-television personality, to do "live" or spontaneous commercials for the condom brand.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong has more Rolls-Royces per head than anywhere else, is the world's leading importer of cognac brandy and has the highest per capita use of cellular phones, according to official statistics.

LONDON - British consumers are increasingly prepared to buy insurance over the Internet, but are not yet ready to buy it from companies based in other European countries, according to a survey by Swiss Re and the Henley research centre.
